RESEARCH NOTES / 003

Know the inputs.

A physical procurement and transport optimizer with a clear boundary between observed benchmarks and estimated network assumptions.

OBSERVED BENCHMARK ≠ ASIAN QUOTE.The saved EIA observation is a U.S. Gulf Coast FOB jet fuel price. The conversion to USD/tonne assumes 0.8 kg/L density. All supply capacities, demands, basis spreads, inventories, reserves, freight, handling and per-tonne storage costs are illustrative estimates. An old observation is labeled stale; an unavailable source falls back to an explicitly estimated input.

Optimization model

The model allocates non-negative quantities across three supply centers and three demand centers. Unit cost is benchmark + supplier basis + shipping + handling + storage. It minimizes total cost subject to supplier and lane capacities and net demand after starting inventory and reserve requirements. If full delivery is impossible, it shows the least-cost partial allocation and unmet demand explicitly.

Demand and capacity are quantities for one user-defined planning period. Distances are not inferred from the map. Transport arcs are schematic. Gulf disruption and Singapore refinery outage are stress-test assumptions, not forecasts or measured exposure estimates.

The comparison baseline is a shipping-cost-first greedy allocation: it fills the cheapest shipping lanes first, without comparing procurement basis or rerouting earlier decisions. Savings are shown only when the optimizer and this baseline both meet all demand. An infeasible or incomplete baseline is not a valid savings denominator. This MVP does not model vessel schedules, lead times, quality blending, financing, taxes, emissions or multi-period storage.

Scope of this MVP

Use it to explore procurement trade-offs, identify capacity bottlenecks and export reproducible scenarios. Connecting audited Asian product prices, terminal inventories, shipping rates and multi-period contracts is the next step toward a commercial energy trading workflow.

No simulated live ticker. No hidden random price changes. Every result is traceable to the visible input scenario.
